title: OPAL: Outlier-Preserved Microscaling Quantization Accelerator for Generative Large Language Models
problem: LLM deployment faces severe memory and bandwidth bottlenecks due to model size growth. While weight quantization has been explored, activation quantization remains largely unaddressed.
motivation: Energy-efficient LLM accelerators are essential to reduce computational and memory burden for practical deployment of increasingly large models.
method: The system quantizes intermediate layer values (activations) into a compact floating-point format with shared exponents across blocks (called microscaling) while preserving 4 uncompressed values per 128-element chunk to maintain accuracy where it matters most. It applies different compression depths based on layer sensitivity: 5-bit encoding for the critical decoder input layers and 3-bit for the rest. Custom hardware handles the preserved values with dedicated floating-point units, processes the bulk of compressed values with vectorized integer multipliers for speed, and optimizes the softmax operation (a mathematical step in language models that normalizes values) by approximating it with only bit-shift and subtraction instead of full computation.
key_novelty: It combines microscaling quantization of activations with selective outlier preservation and compression levels tuned to how much each layer affects the final model accuracy.
contributions: Novel activation quantization method preserving outliers in microscaling format
Mixed-precision strategy targeting layer-specific sensitivity in decoder blocks
Specialized hardware architecture with FP units and vectorized INT multipliers
Log2-based softmax approximation for power efficiency
primary_theme: Quantized LLM inference with outlier preservation
